Q: How to toggle visibility of a Gradio component based on radio button? A:

While I found the answer by @PaulaSema helpful (thank you / upvoted), this answer was created to expand the example to implement DRY for cases where the gr.Textbox is specialised, and enable interactivity with the textbox.

import gradio as gr

with gr.Blocks() as demo:
    radio = gr.Radio(choices=['Hide', 'Show'], label="Show text field:", value='Hide')
    textbox = gr.Textbox(visible=False)

    def update_visibility(radio: gr.Radio):
        """Update textbox visibility."""
        spec = {
                'type': 'text', 
                'placeholder': 'Enter text here ...', 
                'info': 'A brief description of this field\'s use.', 
                'lines': 3,
                'show_label': False,
               }
        bool_ = radio.value == 'Show'
        return gr.Textbox(visible=bool_, interactive=bool_, **spec)

    # Event trigger
    radio.change(fn=update_visibility, inputs=radio, outputs=textbox)

demo.launch(debug=True, share=False)

Additional Notes

  • When providing the gr.Radio type-hint, the object is passed into the function, enabling greater flexibility and object access. If the type-hint is left out, only the .value attribute is passed into the function.
  • The debug=True and share=False arguments have been passed into the demo.launch() function to keep the demo local and enable an easy task kill when running inside an IDE.

Q: How do I extend my Python cash machine program to handle multiple accounts? A:

Since your function doesn't use the arguments pin (it's hardcoded to 4352) and withdrawal_amount (you get it as input later in the function) you could just remove those two arguments and make the function take nothing.

Your new function will not look anything like this. It will have to check the card and find the name and then search through a list of dictionaries to find the right account and get the pin and balance. For what you mention wanting to do next there isn't very much of this that you would reuse.

Q: Link in email with "=ed" being removed from links A:

You are sending a message with the Content-Transfer-Encoding: Quoted-Printable header.

This means everything that starts with = will be considered an escape to insert hexadecimal characters.

=ed will be translated to í in single byte codification ISO-8859-1. Then it is being translated to %EF%BF%BD by the email server since í is a non ASCII character.

I think that is better to use quoted_printable_encode before sending the message content.

Not that you can't use Content-Transfer-Encoding: Quoted-Printable. Just use the proper PHP function to encode the data.

Q: Redemption GetFreeBusy fails with Office 365 (HTTP 401 Autodiscover) in 64-bit Delphi app A:

I am Redemption's author. It does not authenticate with the remote server, the best it can do is intercept and piggyback on credentials used by the MSEMS MAPI provider in the current process. That only works well if the parent process is outlook.exe (i.e. if your code is a COM addin or a VBA script). If it is a standalone exe, there are no credentials to intercept.
